Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, QUEZON CITY Telephone Number 925.11.48 • 925-88.88 • 925.03.32 www.dilg.gov.ph OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG Legal Opinion No. 09A, S. 2013 19 MAR 2013 DIR. FLORIDA M. DIJAN, CESO 111 Regional Director, DILG Region III Diosdado Macapagal Regional Center Maimpis, San Fernando Pampanga Dear Dir. Dijan: This has reference to your letter dated 14 February 2013 requesting a legal opinion on the following queries, to wit: "1) Taking into consideration that the first suspension will end on 20 September 2013 months after election, how will this level treat the subsequent order imposing another period which might probably go beyond September 2013? Stated in another way, will the subsequent order imposing another penalty be followed even if it will be served beyond the duration of the first suspension order? 2) Taking into consideration that suspended Mayor Caspillo is seeking re-election this forth coming Elections, will Aguinaldo Doctrine apply if he wins the elections? Should he be re-elected, will the two suspensions orders be automatically lifted upon taking his oath on 30 June 2013?" As to the first issue, we answer in the negative. In the case of Bautista vs. Primicias, Jr.l, the Supreme Court held that the propriety of the suspension of a Mayor is rendered moot and academic upon the expiration of his/her term and that of the provincial officials who suspended him/her. Based on the foregoing, a local elective official's service of suspension cannot go beyond his term of office. As to the second issue, the case of Malinao vs. Reyes2, citing the landmark case of Aguinaldo vs. Santos3, is instructive, thus: "xxx any administrative disciplinary proceeding against respondent is abated if in the meantime he is reelected, because his reelection results in a condonation of whatever misconduct he might have committed during his previous term. " G.R. No. L-33583 February 12, 1972. G.R. No. 117618 dated 29 March 1996. 212 SCRA 768 (1992). II's more fun in the

In addition thereto, the Supreme Court ruled in the case of Garcia vs. Mojica, et. al.4, in this wise: "In a number of cases, we have repeatedly held that a reelected local official may not be held administratively accountable for misconduct committed during his prior term of office. The rationale for this holding is that when the electorate put him back into office, it is presumed that it did so with full knowledge of his lif& and character, including his past misconduct. If,' armed with such knowledge, it still reelects him, then such reelection is considered a condonation of his past misdeeds. " Since the cases against Mayor Caspillo were filed before the Office of the Ombudsman, the abovementioned Supreme Court rulings in Malinao and Garcia cases should be read in relation to the position Of the Office of the Ombudsman on the matter, the most recent of which was embodied in the 09 March 2012 letter5 of Ombudsman Conchita Carpio-Morales to Atty. Arturo Sicat, Vice-Mayor of Cainta, Rizal, pertinent portion of which reads: "xvx the Doctrine of Condonation is not equally applicable in your case because the Supreme Court has been consistent in its ruling that for condonation to apply, reelection should be to the same position Tor misconduct committed during a 'prior' term. Hence, there is no cogent reason for this Office to deviate from prevailing jurisprudence and this Office is constrained to implement Che penalty imposed pursuant to the Order dated 08 August 2005. " In view thereof, if Mayor Caspillo is re-elected to the same position in the May 2013, the two suspensions implemented against Mayor Caspillo will be dismissed, upon prior manifestation to the Office of the Ombudsman of the fact of his re-election to office. We hope the foregoing sufficiently addresses your concern. V truly yours, AUSTERE ADERO Undersecretary i LS:9 17/11 ('4 4 G.R. No. 139043, 10 September 1999. Copy attached.
